title: Zixin Group sets up joint venture company with ZTO Nongte to operate sweet potato-themed industrial park
article:
Zixin Group (SGX:42W ) (Zixin) announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Hainan Zixin Sweet Potato Industry Technology Co Ltd (Hainan Zixin), has entered into a joint venture agreement with ZTO Agri-Specialty Food Technology (Shandong) Co Ltd (ZTO Nongte).

According to Zixin, this agreement aims to jointly invest in and establish a venture to develop and operate a sweet potato-themed industrial park within the Xinfa Agricultural Industrial Park, located in Liaocheng City, Shandong Province, China.

The proposed joint venture company will have a registered capital of RMB10 million ($1.91 million). ZTO Nongte will have a shareholding of 51% in the joint venture company while Zixin owns the remaining 49% and the capital contribution will be fully paid in accordance to the respective shareholding.

“We believe that this collaborative integration of resources will significantly expedite the replication of our successful business model and act as a catalyst for harnessing and monetising our biotechnological assets and expertise within our existing sweet potato industrial chain,” says Liang Chengwang, executive chairman and CEO of Zixin.

Zixin states that the capital contribution towards the joint venture company will be funded through internal resources and this is not expected to have any material impact on its earnings per share or net tangible assets per share for FY2027 ending March 31.

Shares of Zixin closed unchanged at 3.2 cents on July 22.

title: MLT to divest two China properties to sponsor-led RMB fund; planned disposal of 39 Changi South Avenue 2 for $16.588 mil
article:
The manager of Mapletree Logistics Trust (MLT) (SGX:M44U ) has announced the proposed divestment of two properties in China, Mapletree (Wuxi) Logistics Park (MWLP1) and Mapletree Wuxi New District Logistics Park (MWLP2), to a new Renminbi (RMB) fund led by its sponsor, Mapletree Investment.

The agreed property value stood at RM180 million ($34.3 million) and RMB544 million ($103.6 million) respectively.

MWLP1 comprises three blocks of single-storey warehouses with a net lettable area of 45,084 square metres (sqm) on a land site of about 67,800 sqm. MWLP2 consists of four blocks of two-storey ramp up warehouses with a net lettable area of 122,403 sqm on a land area of almost 100,000 sqm.

Given that the RMB fund is an associate of Mapletree Investment, which is also the controlling unitholder of MLT, this proposed divestment is deemed to be an interested party transaction.

However, given the aggregate value of all transaction entered into MLT with its sponsor, including this proposed divestment, is less than 3% of MLT’s latest audited net asset value and net tangible asset, there is no approval required from MLT’s unitholders.

“Through the RMB Fund, we can unlock value from mature assets and enhance our financial flexibility to pursue new value-accretive investment opportunities. This enables us to continuously optimise and strengthen our portfolio in support of our strategic priorities, while delivering sustainable long-term value for our unitholders,” says Jean Kam, CEO of the manager.

See also: CICT says Paragon reviewing opportunities for AEIs

The manager expects the sales proceeds to be received within six months from the signing of the sales and purchase agreement (SPA) and the proposed divestment is not expected to have a material impact on its net asset value and net property income for FY2027 ending March 31.

At the same time, the manager announced the proposed divestment of 39 Changi South Avenue 2 for a total consideration of $16.588 million. The sales price is 20% above the latest valuation of $13.8 million obtained as at March 31.

Completed in 1997, it is a three-storey cargo lift warehouse with an ancillary office. It has a net lettable area of approximately 6,129 sqm on a land site of approximately 5,212 sqm. Given its relatively small land area, the manager sees limited potential for redevelopment into a modern, ramp-up logistics facility.

See also: S-REITs’ shopping spree pushes 1H2026 acquisitions value to highest since 2021: RHB

The manager says that this proposed divestment is in line with its effort to rejuvenate its portfolio. The proceeds raised from this divestment will be allow the REIT to pursue investment opportunities in modern assets.

Similar to the proposed divestment in China, it is not expected to have a material impact on its net asset value and net property income for FY2027. The proposed divestment is expected to complete by 3QFY2027.

Units of MLT closed 1 cent lower, or 0.83% down at $1.20 on July 22.

title: Norsk Hydro sees aluminium supply risks as gulf flows deteriorate
article:
(July 21): The global aluminium market will face deepening deficits if constraints on shipments through the Strait of Hormuz continue, according to leading European producer Norsk Hydro ASA.

Flows through the critical waterway have deteriorated since the resumption of hostilities between the US and Iran, inhibiting incoming supplies of raw materials and outbound metal exports from the Persian Gulf, Hydro CEO Eivind Kallevik said in an interview.

The Iran war has led smelters in the Middle East, which produce nearly a 10th of the world’s aluminium, to seek out alternative logistic routes, while producers elsewhere are boosting output. But a protracted conflict would drive the market’s supply gap beyond the 900,000-tonne shortfall that Hydro currently expects, Kallevik said.

“It’s quite clear that the situation has deteriorated quite rapidly,” Kallevik said, referring to shipping through Hormuz. “The more protracted the situation in the gulf is, logically the tighter the market will be globally.”

The aluminium market has been roiled by the conflict, with a major reordering of global supply chains helping to blunt some of the impact. China and Indonesia have delivered an unexpected supply boost while other producers, including Norsk Hydro, have also been seeking to ramp up output.

European manufacturers have also been drawing down inventories since the war began, helping to mitigate the impact of outright shortages in the regional market up to now, Kallevik said.

See also: Chile plans US$100 bil copper push to find buyers beyond China

“There was ample supply in many port inventories at the beginning of the year," Kallevik said, noting that incoming shipments had risen ahead of the introduction of a new carbon levy on aluminium imports. “The acid test for the rest of 2026 is how many cargoes we get in to replenish those inventories.”

Production from Norsk Hydro’s recycling operations rose 15% to about 225,000 tonnes over the second quarter, with profitability boosted by a rise in product prices seen as overall supplies tightened. The group’s overall adjusted earnings before items rose 15% year over year to 8.92 billion kroner, beating analysts' estimates.

Aluminium prices on the London Metal Exchange have risen this month as the Middle East conflict escalated, following a slump in June when tensions eased. They were up 0.7% to US$3,180 a tonne as of 11.55am local time.

See also: China seeks stable, transparent mineral rules from Indonesia

Hydro’s shares were up 3.6% in Oslo.
